leadIn: By the end of this lesson, learners will be able to:
objectives: Apply the Partial<T> utility type to make all properties of an interface optional for flexible form handling.
Use the Required<T> utility type to enforce that all properties of a type must be provided when creating objects.
Implement the Readonly<T> utility type to prevent modification of object properties after initialization.
Execute the Pick<T, K> utility type to extract specific properties from a larger interface for focused component props.
Utilize the Omit<T, K> utility type to exclude specific properties from a type when creating derived types.
Construct the Record<K, T> utility type to define objects with consistent property types and dynamic keys.
Apply the Exclude<T, U> utility type to filter out specific union types when creating refined type definitions.
Use the Extract<T, U> utility type to select specific union types that are assignable to another type.
Implement the NonNullable<T> utility type to remove null and undefined from a type for safer property access.
Define function parameters using the Parameters<T> utility type to extract parameter types from function signatures.
Return values using the ReturnType<T> utility type to infer the return type of functions for type-safe assignments.
Modify existing types using the Awaited<T> utility type to unwrap Promise types for handling asynchronous results.
